A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeoRA study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, references and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original mathematical, medical and coding RLVR experiments, together with ablations, mechanism analyses, efficiency measurements and appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and analyses, including the benchmark results in Tables 1–2 and 8 and initialization measurements in Table 7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same spectral/Euclidean mask union, geometry-aware SVD initialization, low-rank adapters and frozen residual. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DeepMath-103K, GSM8K, AlphaMed and Eurus-2-RL-Data training coverage and the same mathematical, medical, coding and out-of-distribution evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. Tables 1 and 8 retain FullFT, SparseFT, LoRA, PiSSA and MiLoRA; Table 2 retains Base, FullFT and LoRA alongside GeoRA.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same model configurations, GRPO setup, data splits, training budgets, decoding settings, verification procedures and evaluation metrics. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Both retain the initialization and mask ablations in Table 4, geometric and spectral analyses in Section 5, learning-rate and stability tests in Figures 4–5, and rank/sparsity sensitivity analysis in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 specifies a single random run in both versions. Neither version reports additional repeated runs, seed lists, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including Tables 1–8 and Figures 3–7. For example, GeoRA's Qwen3-8B AIME24 score remains 23.75 in Table 1, and its training time remains 185 seconds per iteration in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and Appendix B's optimality and function-preservation propositions, gradient derivation and complexity arguments are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about geometry-aware adaptation, training stability, hardware efficiency, cross-domain performance and reduced forgetting.

C2.justification: Interpretations of complementary geometric priors, low-rank update structure and stability are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning initialization overhead and validation beyond the studied architectures and verifiable-reward settings.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain identical initialization, implementation and hardware details, including rank 16, scaling factor 32, sparsity ratio 0.2 and task-specific processing instructions. No reproducibility or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the bibliography are unchanged after matching text across page breaks. GeoRA's positioning relative to existing low-rank and sparse adaptation methods is identical.

P1.justification: v4 adds three first-page footnotes explaining existing author symbols: work during an internship at Meituan, corresponding authors and equal contribution. Scientific prose, section order and terminology are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added author footnotes cause limited column and page reflow, including a vertical shift of Table 3. The version/date stamp changes, while figure and table designs and captions remain unchanged; appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies author attribution through the added footnotes, but retains identical scientific content, results, theory, limitations and reproducibility information, including the appendices. This administrative clarification and the accompanying layout reflow do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
